question: When a reading declares an invariance, how much of the answer is fixed before any data is seen? On one tetrahedron, do the four face mirrors and the three axis swaps generate the same symmetry set? For a matrix built by counting co-occurrences, can any row identify its own labelled item once the matrix is rank one, and does replacing the row argmax by an optimal assignment repair that? For a directed relation network, is the permutation null that preserves the two margins able to see anything except the margins?
level: External exact combinatorics, finite permutations and exact rational arithmetic; every statement decided by exhaustion over a declared finite set; no corpus count and no text imported
domain: The four vertices, six edges and three perfect matchings of a tetrahedron with the Klein four-group of axis swaps and the four face mirrors of the affine Weyl group of type A3; declared nonnegative rank-one matrices with five row and five column weights; declared directed networks of four to six edges with the exact law of the statistic over every permutation of the recipients
quantifiers: All four face mirrors for the Coxeter relations, and every element of the group they generate through Coxeter length twenty
All six edges for the action of the Klein four-group, and every one of the three matchings
Every declared rank-one matrix over the weight sweep for the row-argmax collapse
All one hundred twenty permutations of five indices for the assignment optimum at each of the ten declared perturbation values
Every permutation of the recipients for each declared network, which is the exact null law and not a sample of it
grammar: finite permutations and affine isometries composed exactly
breadth-first shells from the identity in a Cayley graph, which realise the Coxeter length
exact integer matrix minors and exact rational comparisons
exhaustive enumeration of permutations for an exact null law
acceptance: The three axis swaps are exactly the three double transpositions, each determines one perfect matching, each fixes exactly the two edges of its own matching and moves the other four, and they commute pairwise
The Klein four-group has exactly three orbits on the six edges, of size two, and they are the three perfect matchings; its edge action is NOT free and every edge stabiliser has order two

The four face mirrors are involutions, non-adjacent pairs commute, adjacent pairs have product of order three, and their generated group is infinite and larger than twenty-four elements within the declared depth
The origin stabiliser of the closure has exactly twenty-four elements, its Coxeter length distribution is one, three, five, six, five, three, one, and no origin-fixing element has length beyond six
The number of alcoves within Coxeter distance of the fundamental one has a constant fourth difference, so it is a cubic polynomial and the closure tiles without closing
A rank-one matrix puts every row's argmax on the same column, and the same holds throughout the declared weight sweep
The declared rank-one matrix has diagonal share eleven forty-fifths against a chance share of one fifth, an excess of two forty-fifths, with exactly zero row-specific information

For sorted row and column weights the identity is the unique assignment optimum of the rank-one matrix, and for a declared unsorted pair the identity is not an optimum, so the assignment reading is margin-determined rather than alignment-determined

The row-argmax reading first succeeds at perturbation five on the declared grid while the assignment reading already succeeds at perturbation zero, and the per-row threshold has the closed form max of the other column weights over the row's own, minus one
Two declared networks with the same two margins have the same exact null law and different observed reciprocity, so the null can see only the margins
The declared two-way network attains the top of its null support, so a fully reciprocal network is detectable, while the chain's observed value lies inside its null support
protected: No classical text, edition, transcription, commentary, name table or annotation is imported, and no corpus count from any external repository is imported or recomputed here

The matrices and networks in this contract are declared synthetic objects, not measurements of any corpus; the external measurements cited in the note are attributed to their repository and are not re-run here
No claim that the three axis swaps or the four face mirrors are the symmetry of any text, or that any classical scheme is the tetrahedron used here
No claim that a rank-one model is the correct model of any co-occurrence table, only that a rank-one table cannot distinguish its rows
No claim about the statistical significance of any external measurement, and no claim that a permutation test is invalid in general: the statement is about what this family of nulls can see
No claim that the affine Weyl group of type A3 is a native Adva structure or has an implementation, and no connection to the observer, aperture, clock or cell vocabulary
No floating-point value enters any acceptance test
No native Rust witness, no claim promotion beyond bounded-external-experiment, no Seal, no library admission
residual: Three exact statements are established about declared finite objects: a finite symmetry set and its infinite closure differ as groups while sharing the same four faces; a rank-one matrix carries no row-specific information and both the row argmax and the optimal assignment are determined by its margins; and the exact null law of the reciprocity statistic for a permutation of recipients is a function of the two margins alone. Nothing here decides any question about a text. In particular the rank-one result does not show that any real co-occurrence table is rank one, only that the two statistics usually read from it cannot separate a planted labelling from monotone margins; the alignment question the external repository identified remains open and is not settled by any matrix identity. The tetrahedron is a declared combinatorial object and is not claimed to be the scheme of any tradition. The exact null is computed for networks of four to six edges, where every permutation is enumerated; for a network of thousands of edges the same law is not enumerated and no approximation is claimed. The fit of the squared marginal overlap to the exact null mean is reported as an observed ratio on six declared networks, not as a theorem. No statistical claim is made about any external measurement, and none of the cited external numbers is recomputed.
